NVDA.text: Nvidia slipped 0.3% as rising Treasury yields and renewed oil and inflation concerns pushed the Nasdaq down 1.0% and kept pressure on AI-chip shares; no fresh Nvidia-specific catalyst was confirmed.

AVGO.text: Broadcom edged up 0.4%, bucking a 1.0% Nasdaq decline; no fresh Broadcom-specific catalyst was confirmed, making the move a modest rebound after Wednesday's Marvell-Google-driven selloff rather than a broad chip move.

TSM.text: TSM gained 0.9% despite a 1.0% Nasdaq drop and higher yields; no fresh TSM-specific catalyst was confirmed, so the move appears to be relative strength within an otherwise pressured semiconductor tape.

ASML.text: ASML finished nearly flat, down 0.1%, as semiconductor shares remained pressured by rising global yields and AI-spending concerns; no fresh ASML-specific catalyst was confirmed.

KLAC.text: KLA fell 0.8% as the semiconductor complex stayed under pressure from rising yields and AI-spending concerns; no fresh KLA-specific catalyst was confirmed.

INTC.text: Intel slipped 0.7% as higher Treasury yields and broad technology weakness weighed on semiconductors; no fresh Intel-specific catalyst was confirmed during Thursday's session.

MU.text: Micron jumped 4.0% after unveiling Micron Research Labs, a U.S.-based long-horizon R&D hub focused on advanced memory and AI, helping the shares sharply outperform a falling semiconductor market.

TSLA.text: Tesla fell 1.7% as Big Tech sold off in a rising-yield, oil-driven risk-off session; no fresh Tesla-specific catalyst was confirmed.

META.text: Meta was essentially flat, down less than 0.1%, outperforming a 1.0% Nasdaq drop as the broader market sold off on higher yields and oil and inflation concerns; no fresh Meta-specific catalyst was confirmed.

PLTR.text: Palantir slipped 0.7% as higher Treasury yields pressured growth stocks during a broad Nasdaq selloff; no fresh Palantir-specific catalyst was confirmed.

SPCX.text: SpaceX fell 4.0% as a 319 million-share post-IPO unlock expanded tradable supply, while Musk said the next Starship 'catch' milestone was likely months away, adding company-specific pressure.
